What the workbook does not establish

No verified Solis-specific machine sales revenue, parts revenue, parts percentage, dealer margin or return on investment was found. Peer percentages are comparisons only and cannot be applied to Solis.

The Example only tab uses 1,000 parts requests, not 1,000 tractors sold. It estimates staff time capacity and avoidable return costs under stated assumptions. Time valued in euros is not automatically a cash saving.

values: These are money figures from other machinery companies and ITL. AGCO and Titan provide comparisons. Their percentages do not describe Solis. Read Start here first for definitions.
Parts revenue as a share of total sales
Example: the first figure is AGCO tractor sales revenue of USD 8,711.0 million in 2023. That equals USD 8.711 billion, or USD 8,711,000,000. It is not 8,711 tractors and it is not Solis revenue.

Source F02, audited annual report, pages 113–115. Replacement parts exclude separately unidentified service revenue. AGCO sold most of its grain business in November 2024, changing the group revenue mix.
Financial year ended 31 January 2026. Includes agriculture, construction, Europe and Australia. Amounts below are USD millions.

Gross profit means revenue minus the direct costs assigned to that activity, before operating expenses. It is not net profit. Service cost accounting differs from parts. Source F03, pages 31–33. Titan is a dealer group, so its margins cannot be assigned to Solis or an OEM.
International Tractors Limited and the meaning of operating income

ICRA uses operating income for the revenue measure here. It must not be read as operating profit. PAT means profit after tax. One crore equals 10 million Indian rupees: INR 10,021.8 crore equals INR 100,218,000,000. No exchange conversion has been made.

Source F01 reproduces audited ITL indicators. ITL is the company behind the tractor brands; these are not Solis brand or Netherlands figures. The underlying accounts and finance consolidation scope need confirmation.
Other reviewed peers do not disclose a comparable parts percentage

The reviewed disclosures do not isolate parts revenue for these figures. A missing parts split means not available, not zero. Differences in currency, company scope and reporting year prevent direct size or margin comparisons.
